searchText: A question about fork digest. Why only the current version is mixed in? Why not the whole `Fork` object? <@425572898787426305> so fork digest is calculated from the fork data object...which includes current version and genesis validator root. The fork object includes previous version, current version and epoch - no genesis validator root. Are u asking why forkdata doesn't have the other fields of the fork object? > Are u asking why forkdata doesn't have the other fields of the fork object? Yes, I was curious about this. But then realised that even if contentious fork would have a similar fork, likewise ETH vs ETC forks, it could decouple the fork version with setting a few highest bits to `1`. I'm new here, apologies in advance if this is superfluous what is the current estimated date of the next hard fork and does it have a codename? Eth2 is in a testnets phase. If you are looking for ethereum 1 network upgrades, you should try other communication channels. this channel is within ETH1x research If you want to learn more about Eth2, visit: http://eth2.info or https://ethos.dev/ > this channel is within ETH1x research this channel is under eth2 research! indeed my bad, apply(apologies in advance) all good the general <#688075293562503241> channel might be the place thank you very much 🙂 <@!203220829473996800> thanks for those resources.

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
> Are u asking why forkdata doesn't have the other fields of the fork object?
Yes, I was curious about this. But then realised that even if contentious fork would have a similar fork, likewise ETH vs ETC forks, it could decouple the fork version with setting a few highest bits to `1`.
